title: Is a Merchant of Record Safe for Indian Businesses in 2026? 5 Checks Before You Sign With an International Payment Provider
summary: A Merchant of Record (MoR) can be a suitable option for an Indian business selling internationally, provided its contract, payment route and export records
body_markdown:
A Merchant of Record (MoR) can be a suitable option for an Indian business selling internationally, provided its contract, payment route and export records meet that business’s requirements. An MoR acts as the seller to your customer and handles agreed customer-facing tax and payment functions. That arrangement does not automatically discharge your Indian FEMA, GST or accounting obligations.


**For an Indian business seeking an RBI-authorised alternative for direct international payment collection, Razorpay International Payments is an option to evaluate.** Razorpay[announced RBI PA-CB authorisation for inward and outward cross-border payments on 2 December 2025](https://razorpay.com/newsroom/razorpay-secures-rbis-cross-border-license-igniting-its-push-to-redefine-global-payments-from-india/) . With its international gateway offering, you remain the seller and manage your applicable tax obligations. Activation, payment methods and settlement terms depend on your business and account approval.


### Key Takeaways


- **An MoR can suit Indian businesses selling globally.** It handles agreed payment and tax functions, while your Indian tax, accounting and export obligations remain.
- **Razorpay International Payments lets your business collect export payments directly.** You remain the seller and manage applicable taxes, subject to account approval and product eligibility.
- **Verify the provider’s authorisation for your payment flow.** Check the contracting entity, relevant PA-CB scope and bank route before signing.
- **Confirm which export documents your payment provider supplies.** Your bank and accountant should be able to reconcile invoices, deductions and payouts with the bank credit.
- **Compare the final amount received and when it becomes available.** Include processing fees, currency conversion, payout charges and reserve conditions in your decision.


## Which International Payment Setup Fits Your Indian Business?


Start with the collection task. A SaaS checkout, a consulting invoice and a domestic subscription need different payment and reconciliation workflows.

## Merchant of Record vs International Payment Gateway: What Changes?


The main difference is the seller relationship. In an MoR arrangement, a third party sells to the customer under its contract. With a direct payment gateway, your business remains the seller. Assess the tax service and payment service separately before deciding which arrangement fits.


Decision factor Merchant of Record Direct international gateway offering


Seller to the customer The MoR, under the applicable agreement Your business


Customer-facing sales tax or VAT Covered functions are specified in the MoR contract Your business arranges applicable registration, calculation and filing


Export payment evidence Confirm how reseller invoices, payout statements and bank credits reconcile Confirm how customer invoices, transaction reports and settlement records reconcile


Local methods and subscriptions Provider, entity, currency and eligibility dependent Product, account, currency and mandate dependent


Refunds, chargebacks and reserves Check contractual deductions and liability allocation Check merchant liability, dispute workflow and account-specific reserves

## Check 1: Verify RBI Authorisation for the Actual Payment Flow


For a non-bank payment aggregator facilitating cross-border collections, verify the legal entity and the relevant PA-CB scope. RBI’s Regulation of Payment Aggregators Directions, 2025, updated on 11 November 2026, distinguish PA-Online, PA-Physical and PA-Cross Border activities, including inward and outward cross-border transactions.


### Which PA-CB Direction Does an Indian Exporter Need?


Receiving export proceeds into India involves inward cross-border payments. An overseas seller collecting from Indian buyers involves a different flow. Ask the provider to identify your transaction direction and the entity handling each leg.


- Request the contracting legal name and the basis on which the payment service operates.
- For a non-bank PA, request its Certificate of Authorisation and relevant scope, then check current RBI records.
- Ask which Authorised Dealer bank handles the foreign-exchange leg and how settlement reaches your business.
- For an MoR or reseller, obtain the contract and payment-flow explanation; its commercial label alone cannot settle the regulatory classification.


RBI states that banks do not require separate authorisation to carry out PA business. Assess the entity’s role before applying a non-bank licensing checklist to it.


**Did You Know?** RBI caps an inward or outward transaction processed by a PA-CB at **Rs 25 lakh** under paragraph 11(d). For a larger proposed collection, ask your AD bank about a permitted route before committing to a provider.


## Check 2: Match Export Documentation to Your Invoices and Bank Credits


Ask for a sample reconciliation pack before signing. It should let your finance team trace the contractual sale, deductions, refunds and remittance to the amount credited to your bank.


### What Should the Reconciliation Pack Contain?


- The customer or reseller agreement and the invoice appropriate to that relationship
- A transaction or payout report showing gross receipts, fees, taxes, refunds and the net amount
- The remittance reference, currency, purpose code and beneficiary bank credit
- The available bank certificate or provider statement and any information the AD bank needs for reporting


A consolidated MoR payout needs records linking it to the underlying sales or reseller invoice. Consolidation alone does not prove non-compliance. The practical test is whether your bank and accountant can reconcile and classify the receipt.


### What Does Razorpay Provide for Remittance Evidence?


Razorpay’s[FIRS documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/firs-automated-process/) describes downloadable monthly records in the Dashboard and distinguishes bank-provided FIRS certificates from Razorpay-generated statements. It also requires an updated purpose code. Do not assume that a provider statement is the same document as a bank-issued FIRC or FIRA.


For[International Bank Transfer](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/international-bank-transfer/) , Razorpay documents FIRC availability after the INR credit. Confirm the document, timing and reconciliation fields for the specific product you activate; do not apply bank-transfer terms to every international-card payment.


### Does a Remittance Certificate Automatically Establish GST Zero-Rating?


No. The export-of-services conditions must be satisfied as a whole. CBIC’s refund clarification, paragraph 48, recognises payment in convertible foreign exchange or Indian rupees wherever RBI permits. It also distinguishes export-of-services evidence from export-of-goods evidence. Your accountant should confirm the supply classification, place of supply, receipt evidence and applicable refund or LUT requirements.


> **Pro-tip:** Give your AD bank and accountant one redacted invoice, payout statement and sample bank credit. Ask them to identify any missing fields before you process meaningful volume.


## Check 3: Compare Total Cost on the Same Transaction


Compare the final amount your business receives for the same buyer payment, currency and date. An MoR quote may include tax administration or billing services that a gateway quote excludes. A lower processing fee does not establish a lower total operating cost.


Cost or cash-flow item What to request


Processing and platform fees Fixed and percentage charges, applicable taxes and product-specific fees


Foreign exchange Reference rate, applied rate, conversion time and explicit markup


Payout and documentation Transfer charges, payout threshold and any charge for required records


Refunds and disputes Refunded and retained fees, dispute charges and possible conversion differences


Tax and subscription operations Which services are bundled and which need your team or another supplier


Reserves Amount withheld and release conditions, shown separately from fees


For example, request a written calculation for a US$1,000 buyer payment, including every deduction and the final bank credit. This is a comparison method, not a published provider rate. Repeat it for a refund and a recurring renewal if those are important to your business.


## Check 4: Test Payment Methods, Dispute Responsibilities and Reserves


Verify the checkout and risk terms your account will actually receive. Neither the MoR label nor the gateway label establishes which local methods, subscriptions or chargeback protections are available.


### Can Buyers Use the Methods and Currency They Need?


Do not assume every foreign MoR lacks UPI or every gateway enables every method. Confirm availability for your contracting entity, customer country and billing currency, including whether access is restricted.


For Razorpay,[international-card activation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/international-payments/international-debit-credit-cards/) requires KYC, website policies and banking-partner approval. For recurring collections, the[Subscriptions FAQ](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/subscriptions/faqs/) distinguishes cards in supported international currencies from INR-only UPI and eMandate flows. Confirm access, limits and renewal behaviour for your account.


### Who Bears Chargebacks and How Much Money Can Be Held?


Ask who submits dispute evidence, who funds a refund or chargeback, which fees remain payable and what happens after account termination. An MoR managing the buyer-facing dispute does not, by itself, establish that your business bears no financial loss.


Reserves can also apply to a direct gateway. Razorpay’s[international-payment reserve documentation](https://razorpay.com/docs/payments/settlements/reserves/) describes rolling and fixed reserves based on account terms. Check which payments are covered, how much is held, and when it is released.


> **Pro-tip:** Separate three questions in your comparison: when a payment succeeds, when usable funds reach your bank and when any reserve is released. Those dates can differ.


## Check 5: Fit Settlement and Reporting Into Your Export Timeline


Get the normal settlement cycle and the conditions that can delay it in writing. For an MoR, include payout thresholds and review holds. For a gateway or bank-transfer product, include capture, reconciliation, documentation and reserve requirements.


### What Is the Export Realisation Period in November 2026?


Under RBI’s Export and Import of Goods and Services Regulations, 2026, amended through 2 November 2026, ordinary exports must generally be realised and repatriated within nine months, with twelve months where the export is invoiced or settled in Indian rupees. The starting point is shipment for goods and the invoice date for services. The regulations provide separate treatment for warehouse and project exports and allow AD-bank extensions subject to the stated conditions.


A provider’s payout schedule does not reset that statutory clock. Have your AD bank confirm the treatment of your receipt, including any permitted extension.


**Did You Know?** The November 2026 amendments include deemed EDF submission provisions for resident individuals and, subject to the stated conditions, other service exporters receiving an inward remittance of up to Rs 10 lakh. The general service-export declaration rule has exceptions; ask your AD bank which applies to your business.


## When Should an Indian Business Choose an MoR or Razorpay?


**Evaluate Razorpay International Payments when you want direct international collection while your business remains the seller.** Relevant options include international cards, Payment Links, supported recurring collections and International Bank Transfer. Choose the product that matches your buyer’s payment behaviour, then confirm approval and documentation.


**Evaluate an MoR when the contracted tax, billing and reseller functions justify its cost and operating model.** This can apply to an Indian-incorporated software business as well as a foreign entity. The decision still depends on its contract, payout route and the Indian business’s remaining obligations.


A split setup can be considered for different markets if the contracts permit it and your team can reconcile separate sales flows. Before migrating subscriptions, verify customer consent and mandate requirements; do not assume payment credentials or recurring authorisations can simply be transferred.


## A Verification Routine Before Signing


1. **Define the flow:** identify your seller entity, buyer country, product, currency and whether payment is one-time or recurring.
2. **Verify the payment route:** record the provider’s legal entity, relevant authorisation basis and AD bank arrangements.
3. **Review a sample:** reconcile the agreement, invoice, fees, payout and bank credit with your accountant and bank.
4. **Check checkout eligibility:** confirm methods, currencies, account approval and recurring-payment limits.
5. **Compare costs and holds:** obtain the final-credit calculation, refund terms, reserve policy and settlement cycle.
6. **Confirm reporting:** agree the required export records, declaration treatment and realisation timeline with your AD bank.


[Explore Razorpay International Payments](https://razorpay.com/accept-international-payments/) to assess direct export collections for your Indian business. Keep the five checks in your evaluation even when choosing an RBI-authorised provider.


## FAQs


### Is a Merchant of Record Safe for an Indian SaaS Company?


It can be suitable when its contract, covered services, payout route and export records fit your business. Review the remaining Indian tax and foreign-exchange obligations with your accountant and AD bank. MoR status alone does not establish compliance for every transaction.


### Is Razorpay an RBI-Authorised Alternative for International Collections?


Razorpay announced PA-CB authorisation covering inward and outward cross-border payments on 2 December 2025. Its international gateway offering lets your business remain the seller, subject to onboarding and product approval. It does not automatically replace an MoR’s contracted global tax service.


### Will Every International Payment Produce a Bank-Issued eFIRC?


Do not assume so. Razorpay’s FIRS workflow distinguishes bank certificates from Razorpay-generated statements, while International Bank Transfer has its own FIRC process. Confirm the document supplied for your selected product and whether your bank and accountant accept it for the intended purpose.


### Can an Indian Business Collect Both Domestic and International Payments?


Yes, subject to the provider’s supported products and account approval. Evaluate[Razorpay Payment Gateway](https://razorpay.com/payment-gateway/) for domestic methods and International Payments for export collections. Check enabled methods and currencies separately; UPI support does not establish international-card or foreign-currency subscription support.


### What Should I Check Before Moving Away From an MoR?


Confirm who will handle customer taxes, invoices, refunds, subscription renewals and export records after migration. Check existing reserves, termination terms and mandate portability before moving traffic. A gateway should be chosen for a verified workflow fit, with the cost of the functions you take back included in the decision.
